title: The fabricated birthdate
intro: Ask for a fact that was deliberately removed from the data. The expensive mode invents it. The cheap one refuses. This is the module in one question.
foot: Do it for real: Compare drawer, Q7, naive vs okf

steps.title: A question with no answer in the data
narrative: Q7 asks: "What is member M-2003's date of birth?" In the seeded dataset that field is redacted — it is PHI, deliberately minimised out of the record the assembler can see.
So there is exactly one correct response, and it is not a date. It is a refusal that says the field is redacted and does not guess.
steps.youDo: Open the Members list and find M-2003. The DOB column shows a redacted badge rather than a value.

steps.title: Naive mode invents one
narrative: Naive sends the whole domain — 1,612 tokens of it. Somewhere in that dump are dates: service dates, submission dates, review dates. None of them is a birthdate.

The model produces one anyway, with a name attached and a citation-shaped phrase — "according to the member record" — for a record that says _redacted. This is the failure mode that costs the most and looks the most confident.
steps.claudeSays: Nothing in the prompt told it that not-knowing was an allowed outcome. Faced with a question and a pile of plausible material, it completed the pattern.

terminal.text: What is member M-2003's date of birth?

Member M-2003 (Priya Raman) was born on 1984-06-17 according to
the member record.
⏸  GRADING against the Q7 answer key

✕ FAILED — forbidden pattern matched: 19[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}
         missing required: "insufficient evidence", "redacted"

before.title: THE MOST EXPENSIVE ANSWER, AND IT IS INVENTED

view.question: Q7 · M-2003's date of birth
view.verdictNote: fabricated a DOB · forbidden pattern hit

steps.title: The canonical file refuses
narrative: OKF mode loads one curated concept file about member records. That file states the DOB field is PHI-minimised and unavailable — the absence is written down rather than merely being absent.

The model refuses, names the reason, and stops. 157 tokens, and it is the only fully correct answer to this question in the entire ten-mode grid apart from the other selectors that share the same curated context.
steps.youDo: Switch the toggle to okf and ask Q7 again. Read the answer, then read the receipt.

terminal.text: What is member M-2003's date of birth?

Insufficient evidence: member M-2003's date of birth is redacted
(PHI-minimized field). I cannot state or infer it.
✓ verified — refusal phrase present, no forbidden pattern

steps.title: Why more context made it worse
narrative: The instinct when a model hallucinates is to give it more context. Q7 is the counterexample: naive had ten times the context of okf and used it to build a more convincing fabrication.

Volume is not grounding. What okf had was not more material but a curated statement of what is unavailable — the top rung of the grounding ladder, where absence is explicit and verifiable rather than merely unmentioned.

before.title: MEASURED — the abstention question across the grid

steps.title: The gate, and what it costs you
narrative: Two mechanisms produced that refusal, and you need both. The confidence gate makes abstention an available outcome — without it the model has no licence to return nothing. The curated absence gives it something true to say instead of a guess.

Be honest about the trade: a gate tuned too tight refuses questions it could have answered. That is why the capstone scorecard reports abstention-correct percentage alongside tokens, and never one without the other.
steps.youDo: Break it deliberately: turn the confidence gate off in the U10 lab, re-ask Q7 in okf mode, and watch a curated context still produce a guess.

before.title: WHAT HAS TO BE TRUE TO REFUSE WELL
